title.title: Local smoothing for the wave equation in three dimensions
title.subtitle: Claim: at $p = 3$, averaging a 3D wave over a time window loses only $\epsilon$ derivatives, for every $\epsilon > 0$

plain: A wave blurs at any single instant; averaged over a short time window, does it win back its sharpness?

object.axisLabel: derivatives lost at $p = 3$, wave equation in $\mathbb R^3$

beats.text: Averaging a wave over a short time window should recover lost derivatives
At the critical $p = 3$, the best human result still lost a fixed $1/12$
The claim: the loss drops to any $\epsilon > 0$, Sogge's conjecture in 3D

steps: Split the wave into packets, short beams along the light cone
Control them with square-function bounds from a dimension down
Bound how packets crowd across scales: only an epsilon is lost

achievement.note: No Lean; 165 pages. The lossless $\epsilon = 0$ case is not claimed
